questions.text: दो आवेश जिनमें प्रत्येक का आवेश + q है, एक-दूसरे से '2a' दूरी पर स्थित हैं। कोई तीसरा आवेश – 2q इन दोनों के मध्य बिन्दु पर स्थित है। इन निकाय की स्थितिज ऊर्जा है –
questions.text_english: Two charges + q each are kept '2a' distance apart. A third charge – 2q is placed midway between them. The potential energy of the system is –
questions.solution: The system has three pairs: U(q,q) between the two +q charges separated by 2a, and two U(q,–2q) pairs each between a +q charge and the –2q charge at distance a. U = kq²/(2a) + k(q)(–2q)/a + k(q)(–2q)/a = kq²/(2a) – 2kq²/a – 2kq²/a = kq²/(2a) – 4kq²/a = (1/8πε₀)[q²/(2a) – 4q²/a] = (1/8πε₀a)[q²/2 – 4q²] = (1/8πε₀a)(–7q²/2). Rewriting with denominator 8πε₀a gives –7q²/(8πε₀a). Options A and D are positive, so they cannot be correct since the –2q charge makes the energy negative. Option B gives –6q², which does not match the calculation. Option C, –7q²/(8πε₀a), is the correct result.
questions.topic: Potential Energy of a System of Charges

questions.text: दो सर्वसम लघु चालक गेंदों B₁ और B₂ को क्रमशः –7 pC और + 4 pC आवेश दिए गए हैं। इन दोनों को किसी तीसरी सर्वसम गेंद B₃ द्वारा सम्पर्क में लाकर फिर पृथक कर दिया गया है। अब यदि सभी गेंदों पर अन्तिम आवेश –2 pC है, तो B₃ पर प्रारम्भिक आवेश क्या था?
questions.text_english: Two identical small conducting balls B₁ and B₂ are given –7 pC and + 4 pC charges respectively. They are brought in contact with a third identical ball B₃ and then separated. If the final charge on each ball is –2 pC, the initial charge on B₃ was
questions.solution: By conservation of charge, the total charge before and after contact must be equal. The final charge on each of the three balls is –2 pC, so total final charge = 3 × (–2) = –6 pC. The total initial charge = (–7) + (+4) + Q₃ = –6 pC, where Q₃ is the initial charge on B₃. Solving: –3 + Q₃ = –6, so Q₃ = –3 pC. Option A (–2 pC) gives total –5 pC, option C (–5 pC) gives –8 pC, and option D (–15 pC) gives –18 pC, none of which equal –6 pC. Therefore option B, –3 pC, is correct.

questions.text: प्रकाश की क्वान्टम प्रकृति प्रकाशविद्युत प्रभाव की व्याख्या इस प्रकार करती है –
questions.text_english: The quantum nature of light explains the observations on photoelectric effect as –

options.A: आपतित विकिरणों की कोई निम्नतम आवृत्ति होती है जिससे कम पर कोई इलेक्ट्रॉन उत्सर्जित नहीं होते।
options.B: फोटो-इलेक्ट्रॉनों की अधिकतम गतिज ऊर्जा केवल आपतित विकिरणों की आवृत्ति पर निर्भर करती है।
options.C: जब धातु-पृष्ठ को प्रदीप्त किया जाता है तो कुछ समय पश्चात् पृष्ठ से इलेक्ट्रॉन उत्सर्जित होते हैं।
options.D: प्रकाश विद्युत धारा आपतित विकिरणों की तीव्रता पर निर्भर नहीं करती है।

options_english.A: there is a minimum frequency of incident radiation below which no electrons are emitted.
options_english.B: the maximum kinetic energy of photoelectrons depends only on the frequency of incident radiation.
options_english.C: when the metal surface is illuminated, electrons are ejected from the surface after sometime.
options_english.D: the photoelectric current is independent of the intensity of incident radiation.

questions.solution: According to Einstein's photon theory, each photon carries energy E = hν. An electron absorbs one photon and uses part of it to overcome the work function; the rest becomes kinetic energy: KE_max = hν – φ. This directly explains why maximum kinetic energy depends only on frequency, not on intensity. Option A describes the threshold frequency, which is a correct experimental observation but is a consequence of the work function concept, not the primary quantum explanation. Option C is incorrect because emission is essentially instantaneous (no time delay) — this is actually explained by the quantum nature, but the statement says 'after sometime', which is wrong. Option D is incorrect because photoelectric current does depend on intensity (more photons = more electrons). Therefore option B is the correct explanation provided by the quantum nature of light.
questions.chapter: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter

questions.text: हाइड्रोजन परमाणु के बोर-मॉडल में nवीं कक्षा की त्रिज्या (rₙ) n के साथ किस प्रकार विचरण करती है?
questions.text_english: The radius (rₙ) of nth orbit in Bohr model of hydrogen atom varies with n as
questions.solution: In Bohr's model, the radius of the nth orbit is given by rₙ = n²h²ε₀/(πme²) = n² × a₀, where a₀ = 0.529 Å is the Bohr radius. This formula clearly shows rₙ ∝ n². Option A (rₙ ∝ n) is incorrect as the dependence is quadratic, not linear. Options B and D involve inverse relationships which would mean larger orbits at smaller n, contradicting the model. Option C is therefore the correct answer.

questions.text: किसी सीधे तार को पूर्व-पश्चिम दिशा के अनुदिश क्षैतिजत: रखा गया है। यदि इस तार से पूर्व से पश्चिम दिशा में कोई अचर धारा प्रवाहित की जाए, तो बिंदु पर तार के ऊपर चुम्बकीय क्षेत्र की दिशा किस ओर होगी?
questions.text_english: A straight wire is kept horizontally along east-west direction. If a steady current flows in wire from east to west, the magnetic field at a point above the wire will point towards
questions.solution: Using the right-hand thumb rule: point the thumb of the right hand in the direction of current flow (east to west, i.e., in the –x direction). The fingers curl to show the direction of the magnetic field. Above the wire, the curling fingers point towards the North direction. Options A and B (east and west) lie along the wire axis and are not the field direction. Option D (south) would be correct below the wire. Therefore, option C (North) is correct.
questions.topic: Magnetic Field due to a Straight Wire

questions.text: किसी प्रतिचुम्बकीय पदार्थ की चुम्बकीय प्रवृत्ति होती है
questions.text_english: The magnetic susceptibility for a diamagnetic material is
questions.solution: Diamagnetic materials are weakly repelled by magnetic fields. Their magnetic susceptibility χ is small and negative (typically of the order –10⁻⁵ to –10⁻⁶). The negative sign indicates that magnetisation opposes the applied field. Option B describes paramagnetic materials (small and positive χ). Options C and D describe ferromagnetic materials which have large susceptibility. Therefore option A is correct.

questions.text: किसी गैल्वेनोमीटर को जिसका प्रतिरोध 100 Ω है, 0.1 Ω के प्रतिरोध का उपयोग करके (0–1 A) परिसर के एमीटर में परिवर्तित किया गया है। यह जिस धारा के लिए पूर्ण पैमाना विक्षेपण दर्शाएगा, वह धारा है लगभग
questions.text_english: A galvanometer of resistance 100 Ω is converted into an ammeter of range (0–1 A) using a resistance of 0.1 Ω. The ammeter will show full scale deflection for a current of about
questions.solution: For an ammeter conversion, the shunt resistance S = G·Iₘ/(I – Iₘ), where G is galvanometer resistance, Iₘ is full-scale deflection current of galvanometer, and I is the desired range. Rearranging: Iₘ = I·S/(G+S) = 1 × 0.1/(100 + 0.1) ≈ 0.1/100.1 ≈ 1 mA. This means the galvanometer itself deflects full scale at approximately 1 mA. Options A (0.1 mA), C (10 mA), and D (0.1 A) do not satisfy the shunt equation for the given values. Therefore option B, 1 mA, is correct.

questions.text: त्रिज्या R के किसी वृत्ताकार पाश A से कोई धारा I प्रवाहित हो रही है। त्रिज्या r (= R/20) के किसी वृत्ताकार पाश B को A के तल में संकेन्द्री रखा गया है। पाश B से संबद्ध चुम्बकीय फ्लक्स निम्नलिखित में से किसके अनुक्रमानुपाती है?
questions.text_english: A circular loop A of radius R carries a current I. Another circular loop B of radius r (= R/20) is placed concentrically in the plane of A. The magnetic flux linked with loop B is proportional to
questions.solution: The magnetic field at the centre of loop A is B = μ₀I/(2R). Since loop B is very small (r = R/20 ≪ R), the field over its area can be taken as uniform and equal to the central field. The flux through B is Φ = B × πr² = [μ₀I/(2R)] × π(R/20)² = μ₀Iπ/(2R) × R²/400 = μ₀IπR/800. Thus Φ ∝ R, making option A correct. Options B, C, and D suggest different power-law dependencies which do not arise from this calculation.

questions.text: आरेख में दो आदर्श प्रेरकों, जिनके प्रेरकत्व L₁ और L₂ हैं, के प्रेरकीय प्रतिघात X_L का कोणीय आवृत्ति ω के साथ विचरण दर्शाया गया है। L₁/L₂ का मान है –
questions.text_english: Figure shows the variation of inductive reactance X_L of two ideal inductors of inductance L₁ and L₂, with angular frequency ω. The value of L₁/L₂ is
questions.solution: The inductive reactance is X_L = Lω, so the slope of the X_L vs ω graph equals the inductance L. The slope is tan(θ) where θ is the angle with the ω-axis. From the graph, L₂ has slope tan60° = √3 and L₁ has slope tan30° = 1/√3. Therefore L₁/L₂ = (1/√3)/√3 = 1/3. Options A, B, and C do not match this ratio. Option D, 1/3, is correct.

questions.text: z-अक्ष के अनुदिश संचरण करती किसी विद्युत चुम्बकीय तरंग के विद्युत क्षेत्र E→ और चुम्बकीय क्षेत्र B→ के बीच कलान्तर होता है –
questions.text_english: The phase difference between electric field E→ and magnetic field B→ in an electromagnetic wave propagating along z-axis is –
questions.solution: In an electromagnetic wave, the electric field E and magnetic field B oscillate in phase with each other. Both reach their maximum, minimum, and zero values at the same instant and at the same position. This is a fundamental property of electromagnetic waves derived from Maxwell's equations. Options B (π), C (π/2), and D (π/4) all imply a phase difference between E and B, which is incorrect. Therefore option A, zero phase difference, is correct.

questions.text: N फेरों की कोई कुण्डली किसी चुम्बकीय क्षेत्र B→ में इस प्रकार स्थित है कि चुम्बकीय क्षेत्र B→ कुण्डली के तल के लम्बवत् है। B→ में समय के साथ B = B₀ cos(2π/T · t) के रूप में परिवर्तन होता है, यहाँ T आवर्तकाल है। कुण्डली में प्रेरित emf का परिमाण जिस समय पर अधिकतम होगा वह है
questions.text_english: A coil of N turns is placed in a magnetic field B→ such that B→ is perpendicular to the plane of the coil. B→ changes with time as B = B₀ cos(2π/T · t) where T is time period. The magnitude of emf induced in the coil will be maximum at
questions.solution: The magnetic flux is Φ = NBA cos(2πt/T). The induced emf is e = –dΦ/dt = NBA(2π/T)sin(2πt/T). The emf is maximum when sin(2πt/T) = ±1, i.e., when 2πt/T = π/2, 3π/2, 5π/2, ... which gives t = T/4, 3T/4, 5T/4, ... These values can be written as t = (2n–1)T/4. Among the given options, t = nT/2 gives t = T/2, T, 3T/2, ... At t = T/2: sin(π) = 0, so emf = 0. At t = nT/4 with n odd these coincide. The emf is maximum when sin = ±1, which occurs at t = T/4, 3T/4 etc., best captured by option C: t = nT/2 does not universally give maximum. Re-examining: at t = nT/2, sin(2π·nT/2·1/T) = sin(nπ) = 0, giving minimum emf. At t = nT/4, sin(nπ/2) = ±1 for odd n, giving maximum. Therefore option B, t = nT/4, is the correct answer.

questions.text: हाइड्रोजन परमाणु की बामर श्रेणी में, जैसे ही स्पेक्ट्रमी रेखाओं की तरंगदैर्घ्य घटती है वह प्रतीत होती हैं
questions.text_english: In Balmer series of hydrogen atom, as the wavelength of spectral lines decreases, they appear

options.B: एक-दूसरे से अधिक दूरी पर तथा तीव्रता में अधिक प्रबल
options.C: एक-दूसरे के निकट दूरी पर तथा तीव्रता में अधिक प्रबल
options.D: एक-दूसरे के निकट दूरी पर तथा तीव्रता में अधिक दुर्बल

options_english.B: further apart and stronger in intensity.
options_english.C: closer together and stronger in intensity.
options_english.D: closer together and weaker in intensity.

questions.solution: In the Balmer series, spectral lines converge toward the series limit (364.6 nm) as the wavelength decreases, meaning the lines get closer together. Higher-energy transitions (larger n to n=2) are less probable and correspond to higher energy levels which are more densely packed, resulting in weaker intensity. Options A and B are incorrect as lines are not equally spaced and do not move further apart. Option C is wrong because intensity decreases, not increases, as wavelength decreases. Option D correctly states that the lines appear closer together and weaker in intensity.

questions.text:
अभिकथन (A): पीले प्रकाश द्वारा किरणित किए जाने पर जिंक के पृष्ठ से इलेक्ट्रॉनों का उत्सर्जन होता है।
कारण (R): जिंक के कार्यफलन की तुलना में पीले प्रकाश के फोटॉन से संबद्ध ऊर्जा अधिक होती है।
questions.text_english:
Assertion (A): Electrons are ejected from the surface of zinc when it is irradiated by yellow light.
Reason (R): Energy associated with a photon of yellow light is more than the work function of zinc.
questions.instruction_line: प्रश्न संख्या 13 से 16 में दो कथन दिए गए हैं – एक को अभिकथन (A) तथा दूसरे को कारण (R) लेबल किया गया है।
questions.instruction_line_english: For questions 13 to 16, two statements are given – one labelled Assertion (A) and the other labelled Reason (R). Select the correct answer from codes (A), (B), (C) and (D).

options.A: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सत्य हैं और कारण (R) अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या है।
options.B: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सत्य हैं और कारण (R) अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या नहीं है।
options.C: अभिकथन (A) सत्य है और कारण (R) असत्य है।
options.D: यदि दोनों अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) असत्य हैं।

options_english.A: If both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
options_english.B: If both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
options_english.C: If Assertion (A) is true and Reason (R) is false.
options_english.D: If both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are false.

questions.solution: The work function of zinc is approximately 4.3 eV. The energy of a photon of yellow light (wavelength ≈ 580 nm) is E = hc/λ ≈ (6.63×10⁻³⁴ × 3×10⁸)/(580×10⁻⁹) ≈ 2.1 eV. Since 2.1 eV < 4.3 eV, yellow light cannot eject electrons from zinc. Therefore, Assertion (A) is false — zinc does not emit electrons under yellow light. Reason (R) is also false because the photon energy of yellow light is less than, not more than, the work function of zinc. Hence both A and R are false, and option D is correct.
questions.chapter: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter

questions.text:
अभिकथन (A): धातुओं के लिए प्रतिरोध ताप गुणांक धनात्मक तथा p-प्रकार के अर्धचालकों के लिए प्रतिरोध ताप गुणांक ऋणात्मक होता है।
कारण (R): धातुओं में आवेश वाहक ऋणावेशित होते हैं जबकि p-प्रकार के अर्धचालकों में बहुसंख्यक आवेश वाहक धनावेशित होते हैं।
questions.text_english:
Assertion (A): The temperature coefficient of resistance is positive for metals and negative for p-type semiconductors.
Reason (R): The charge carriers in metals are negatively charged, whereas the majority charge carriers in p-type semiconductors are positively charged.

options.A: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सत्य हैं और कारण (R) अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या है।
options.B: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सत्य हैं और कारण (R) अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या नहीं है।
options.C: अभिकथन (A) सत्य है और कारण (R) असत्य है।
options.D: यदि दोनों अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) असत्य हैं।

options_english.A: If both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
options_english.B: If both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
options_english.C: If Assertion (A) is true and Reason (R) is false.
options_english.D: If both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are false.

questions.solution: Assertion (A) is true: metals have a positive temperature coefficient of resistance because rising temperature increases lattice vibrations and thus increases resistance. P-type semiconductors have a negative temperature coefficient because increasing temperature generates more electron-hole pairs, increasing conductivity and decreasing resistance. Reason (R) is also true: metals conduct via free electrons (negatively charged) and p-type semiconductors have holes (positively charged) as majority carriers. However, R does not explain the sign of the temperature coefficient — the sign depends on whether carriers increase or decrease with temperature, not on the sign of the charge of the carriers. Therefore both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A, making option B correct.

questions.text:
अभिकथन (A): जब किसी चालक में इलेक्ट्रॉन का अपवाह होता है तो इसका यह अर्थ नहीं होता है कि उस चालक के सभी मुक्त इलेक्ट्रॉन समान दिशा में गतिमान हैं।
कारण (R): अपवाह वेग इलेक्ट्रॉनों के बृहत् यादृच्छिक वेगों पर अध्यारोपित होता है।
questions.text_english:
Assertion (A): When electrons drift in a conductor, it does not mean that all free electrons in the conductor are moving in the same direction.
Reason (R): The drift velocity is superposed over large random velocities of electrons.

options.A: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सत्य हैं और कारण (R) अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या है।
options.B: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सत्य हैं और कारण (R) अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या नहीं है।
options.C: अभिकथन (A) सत्य है और कारण (R) असत्य है।
options.D: यदि दोनों अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) असत्य हैं।

options_english.A: If both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
options_english.B: If both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
options_english.C: If Assertion (A) is true and Reason (R) is false.
options_english.D: If both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are false.

questions.solution: Assertion (A) is true: in a conductor, free electrons have large random thermal velocities in all directions. When an electric field is applied, a small drift velocity is superimposed on these random motions. At any instant, different electrons move in different random directions; only their net average displacement is along the field direction. Reason (R) is also true and correctly explains A: the drift velocity (~10⁻³ m/s) is much smaller than the random thermal velocity (~10⁶ m/s), and since it is merely superposed on the random motion, individual electrons do not all move in the same direction at a given instant. Both statements are true and R is the correct explanation of A, so option A is correct.

questions.text:
अभिकथन (A): प्रकाश के व्यतिकरण और विवर्तन में प्रकाश ऊर्जा एक प्रदेश में घट जाती है और कोई काली फ्रिंज उत्पन्न करती है। किसी अन्य प्रदेश में यह बढ़ जाती है और कोई चमकीली फ्रिंज उत्पन्न करती है।
कारण (R): ऐसा इस कारण से होता है, क्योंकि व्यतिकरण और विवर्तन की परिघटनाओं में ऊर्जा का संरक्षण नहीं होता है।
questions.text_english:
Assertion (A): In interference and diffraction of light, light energy reduces in one region producing a dark fringe. It increases in another region and produces a bright fringe.
Reason (R): This happens because energy is not conserved in the phenomena of interference and diffraction.

options.A: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सत्य हैं और कारण (R) अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या है।
options.B: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सत्य हैं और कारण (R) अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या नहीं है।
options.C: अभिकथन (A) सत्य है और कारण (R) असत्य है।
options.D: यदि दोनों अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) असत्य हैं।

options_english.A: If both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
options_english.B: If both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
options_english.C: If Assertion (A) is true and Reason (R) is false.
options_english.D: If both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are false.

questions.solution: Assertion (A) is true: in interference and diffraction patterns, energy is redistributed — dark fringes have zero or reduced intensity while bright fringes have enhanced intensity. However, the total energy across the entire pattern is conserved; it is merely redistributed in space. Reason (R) is false: energy IS conserved in interference and diffraction. The energy lost at dark fringes is gained at bright fringes. The redistribution happens due to the superposition principle, not due to non-conservation of energy. Therefore A is true but R is false, making option C correct.

questions.text: किसी p-n संधि डायोड का (i) अग्रदिशिक बायसन और (ii) पश्चदिशिक बायसन में परिपथ आरेख खींचिए। इन दोनों प्रकरणों में I-V अभिलाक्षणिक भी खींचिए।
questions.text_english: Draw the circuit diagram of a p-n junction diode in (i) forward biasing and (ii) reverse biasing. Also draw its I-V characteristics in the two cases.

key_points: Forward bias circuit: positive terminal of battery connected to p-side, negative terminal to n-side; I-V graph shows exponential rise after threshold (~0.7V for Si)
Reverse bias circuit: positive terminal connected to n-side, negative to p-side; I-V graph shows tiny reverse saturation current until breakdown voltage

questions.solution: In forward biasing, the positive terminal of the battery is connected to the p-side and the negative terminal to the n-side of the p-n junction diode. The potential barrier is reduced, allowing majority carriers to cross the junction, so current increases exponentially beyond the threshold voltage (about 0.3 V for Ge, 0.7 V for Si). In reverse biasing, the connections are reversed: positive to n-side and negative to p-side. The potential barrier increases and only a very small reverse saturation current (due to minority carriers) flows, which remains nearly constant until the reverse breakdown voltage is reached, after which the current increases sharply. The I-V characteristic curve has a steep exponential rise in the first quadrant (forward bias) and a nearly flat, very small current in the third quadrant until the breakdown point (reverse bias).
questions.topic: p-n Junction Diode and I-V Characteristics

questions.text: किसी प्रोटॉन और किसी अल्फा कण को विभिन्न विभवों क्रमश: V₁ और V₂ के द्वारा इस प्रकार त्वरित किया गया है ताकि इन दोनों की दे ब्रोग्ली तरंगदैर्ध्य समान हों। V₁/V₂ ज्ञात कीजिए।
questions.text_english: A proton and α-particle are accelerated through different potentials V₁ and V₂ respectively so that they have the same de Broglie wavelengths. Find V₁/V₂.

key_points: de Broglie wavelength after acceleration: λ = h/√(2mqV)
For equal wavelengths: m_p q_p V₁ = m_α q_α V₂
V₁/V₂ = (m_α q_α)/(m_p q_p) = (4m_p × 2e)/(m_p × e) = 8

questions.solution: The de Broglie wavelength of a particle accelerated through potential V is λ = h/√(2mqV), where m is mass and q is charge. For equal wavelengths of the proton and alpha particle: h/√(2m_p q_p V₁) = h/√(2m_α q_α V₂), which gives m_p q_p V₁ = m_α q_α V₂. The alpha particle has mass m_α = 4m_p and charge q_α = 2e, while the proton has mass m_p and charge q_p = e. Therefore V₁/V₂ = (m_α q_α)/(m_p q_p) = (4m_p × 2e)/(m_p × e) = 8. Hence V₁/V₂ = 8.
questions.chapter: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter

questions.text: कोई प्रकाश किरण अपवर्तनांक μ के समबाहु काँच के प्रिज्म के फलक पर अभिलम्बवत् आपतन करती है। जब इस प्रिज्म को किसी पारदर्शी माध्यम में पूर्णतः डुबोया जाता है तो यह प्रेक्षण किया जाता है कि निर्गत किरण संलग्न फलक को ठीक-ठीक स्पर्श करती है। इस माध्यम का अपवर्तनांक ज्ञात कीजिए।
questions.text_english: A ray of light is incident normally on one face of an equilateral glass prism of refractive index μ. When the prism is completely immersed in a transparent medium, it is observed that the emergent ray just grazes the adjacent face. Find the refractive index of the medium.

key_points: Ray enters normally, travels inside, hits second face at 60° (equilateral prism)
Emergent ray grazes adjacent face means angle of refraction = 90°, so angle of incidence at second surface = critical angle θ_c
sin θ_c = n_medium/μ, and θ_c = 60°, so n_medium = μ sin 60° = μ√3/2

questions.solution: Since the ray is incident normally on the first face of the equilateral prism, it passes through without refraction. Inside the prism, it travels and strikes the second face at an angle of incidence equal to 60° (since all angles of an equilateral prism are 60°). The emergent ray just grazes the second face, meaning the angle of refraction at the second face is 90°. This condition implies that 60° is exactly the critical angle for the glass–medium interface. Applying Snell's law at the second face: μ sin60° = n_medium × sin90°, so n_medium = μ sin60° = μ√3/2.
questions.topic: Total Internal Reflection and Critical Angle

questions.text: वोल्टता V पर दो विद्युत हीटरों के शक्ति अनुमतांक P₁ और P₂ हैं। इन दोनों को dc वोल्टता V से श्रेणी में संयोजित किया गया है। दोनों के संयोजन द्वारा उपभुक्त शक्ति ज्ञात कीजिए। यदि इन दोनों को समान स्रोत से पार्श्व में संयोजित किया जाए, तो क्या ये दोनों समान शक्ति उपभुक्त करेंगी?
questions.text_english: Two electric heaters have power ratings P₁ and P₂, at voltage V. They are connected in series to a dc source of voltage V. Find the power consumed by the combination. Will they consume the same power if connected in parallel across the same source?

key_points: Resistance of each heater: R₁ = V²/P₁, R₂ = V²/P₂
Series power: P_series = V²/(R₁+R₂) = P₁P₂/(P₁+P₂)
Parallel power: P_parallel = P₁+P₂, which is different from series power

questions.solution: The resistance of heater 1 is R₁ = V²/P₁ and of heater 2 is R₂ = V²/P₂. In series, total resistance = R₁ + R₂ = V²(P₁+P₂)/(P₁P₂). The power consumed by the series combination is P_series = V²/(R₁+R₂) = P₁P₂/(P₁+P₂). In parallel across the same source V, each heater operates at its rated voltage, so the total power is P_parallel = P₁+P₂. Since P₁P₂/(P₁+P₂) ≠ P₁+P₂ in general, no, they will not consume the same power when connected in parallel as when connected in series.
questions.topic: Power in Series and Parallel Circuits

questions.text: (a) आरेख में दर्शाए अनुसार अपवर्तनांक 1.5 और त्रिज्या 40 cm के किसी काँच के गोले में कोई वायु का बुलबुला बिन्दु B (CB = 20 cm) पर फंस गया है। बिन्दु P से प्रेक्षण करने पर इस बुलबुले के प्रतिबिम्ब की प्रकृति और स्थिति ज्ञात कीजिए।
questions.text_english: (a) An air bubble is trapped at point B (CB = 20 cm) in a glass sphere of radius 40 cm and refractive index 1.5 as shown in figure. Find the nature and position of the image of the bubble as seen by an observer at point P.

sub_questions.text: किसी अपवर्ती दूरदर्शक के सामान्य समायोजन में अभिदृश्यक और अभिनेत्र लेंस के बीच की दूरी 1.00 m है। यदि इस दूरदर्शक की आवर्धन क्षमता 19 है, तो अभिदृश्यक और अभिनेत्र लेंस की फोकस दूरी ज्ञात कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: In normal adjustment, for a refracting telescope, the distance between objective and eye piece lens is 1.00 m. If the magnifying power of the telescope is 19, find the focal length of the objective and the eyepiece lens.

key_points: In normal adjustment: f_o + f_e = 1.00 m and M = f_o/f_e = 19
From M = 19: f_o = 19f_e; substituting: 19f_e + f_e = 1.00 m, so f_e = 0.05 m = 5 cm

sub_questions.solution: In normal adjustment of a refracting telescope, the separation between objective and eyepiece equals f_o + f_e = 1.00 m. The magnifying power is M = f_o/f_e = 19, giving f_o = 19f_e. Substituting into the distance equation: 19f_e + f_e = 1.00 m, so 20f_e = 1.00 m, hence f_e = 0.05 m = 5 cm and f_o = 19 × 5 = 95 cm.

key_points: Apply refraction at spherical surface formula for near face: n₂/v – n₁/u = (n₂–n₁)/R
Object is at B, 20 cm from centre, so distance from near surface = 40–20 = 20 cm inside glass; u = –20 cm (from near surface to observer side), n₁=1.5 (glass), n₂=1 (air), R = –40 cm
Image forms at v = –20 cm from the near surface, i.e., virtual image inside the sphere

questions.solution: The air bubble at B is 20 cm from the centre C. The observer is at P, to the left. We first apply refraction at the left spherical surface. For the left surface, the object (bubble) is in glass (n₁ = 1.5) at a distance of 40 – 20 = 20 cm from the surface, so u = –20 cm. The surface is concave toward the observer, R = –40 cm, and n₂ = 1 (air). Using n₂/v – n₁/u = (n₂–n₁)/R: 1/v – 1.5/(–20) = (1–1.5)/(–40), giving 1/v + 0.075 = 0.0125, so 1/v = –0.0625, v = –16 cm. The negative sign indicates a virtual image located 16 cm to the left of the left surface, i.e., outside the glass sphere, at 16 cm from the surface. The image is virtual and erect.

questions.text:
(a) नाभिकीय विखण्डन और नाभिकीय संलयन के बीच विभेदन कीजिए।
(b) ₉₄Pu²³⁹ के विखण्डन गुणों और ₉₂U²³⁵ के विखण्डन-गुणों में अत्यधिक समानता है। यदि शुद्ध ₉₄Pu²³⁹ के 1 g के सभी परमाणुओं का विखण्डन हो जाए, तो कितनी ऊर्जा (MeV में) मुक्त होगी? प्रति विखण्डन मुक्त औसत ऊर्जा 180 MeV है।
questions.text_english:
(a) Differentiate between nuclear fission and fusion.
(b) The fission properties of ₉₄Pu²³⁹ are very similar to those of ₉₂U²³⁵. How much energy (in MeV), is released if all the atoms in 1 g of pure ₉₄Pu²³⁹ undergo fission? The average energy released per fission is 180 MeV.

key_points: Fission: heavy nucleus splits into two lighter nuclei releasing ~200 MeV; fusion: light nuclei combine to form heavier nucleus releasing ~17 MeV per reaction
Number of atoms in 1g of Pu-239 = (6.023×10²³/239)
Total energy = (6.023×10²³/239) × 180 MeV ≈ 4.53×10²³ MeV

questions.solution: Nuclear fission is the process in which a heavy nucleus (like U-235 or Pu-239) splits into two medium-mass nuclei with the release of a large amount of energy (~200 MeV per fission) and 2–3 neutrons. It is initiated by neutron bombardment. Nuclear fusion is the process in which two light nuclei (like deuterium and tritium) combine at very high temperatures and pressures to form a heavier nucleus, releasing energy (~17 MeV per reaction). Fission produces radioactive waste while fusion produces less harmful products. For part (b): number of atoms in 1 g of Pu-239 = (6.023 × 10²³)/239 ≈ 2.52 × 10²¹ atoms. Total energy released = 2.52 × 10²¹ × 180 MeV ≈ 4.53 × 10²³ MeV.

questions.text: किसी प्रदेश में विद्युत क्षेत्र इस प्रकार दिया गया है – E→ = (10x + 4) î, यहाँ x को m तथा E को N/C में लिया गया है। किया गया कार्य परिकलित कीजिए, जबकि किसी मात्रक आवेश को ले जाया गया है (i) (5 m, 0) से (10 m, 0) तक (ii) (5 m, 0) से (5 m, 10 m) तक
questions.text_english: The electric field in a region is given by E→ = (10x + 4) î where x is in m and E is in N/C. Calculate the amount of work done in taking a unit charge from (i) (5 m, 0) to (10 m, 0) (ii) (5 m, 0) to (5 m, 10 m)

key_points: Work done W = q∫E·dl; for unit charge W = ∫E dx along path
(ii) Path is along y-axis at x=5; E is along x-direction, displacement along y, E·dl=0, so W=0

questions.solution: The electric field is E→ = (10x + 4) î N/C, directed along the x-axis. Work done in moving a unit charge is W = ∫E→·dl→. For part (i), the displacement is along the x-axis from x = 5 m to x = 10 m: W = ∫₅¹⁰(10x + 4)dx = [5x² + 4x]₅¹⁰ = (5×100 + 40) – (5×25 + 20) = 540 – 145 = 395 J. For part (ii), the displacement is from (5, 0) to (5, 10), which is entirely along the y-axis at constant x = 5 m. Since E→ is along î (x-direction) and the displacement dl→ is along ĵ (y-direction), E→·dl→ = 0 throughout. Therefore W = 0.

questions.text: गाइगर मार्शडेन प्रयोग में प्रकीर्णन कोण (θ) के साथ संसूचित प्रकीर्णित कणों (N) के विचरण को दर्शाने के लिए ग्राफ खींचिए। इस ग्राफ द्वारा आप जिन दो निष्कर्षों को निकाल सकते हैं, उन्हें लिखिए। इस प्रयोग में उपगमन की निकटतम दूरी के लिए व्यंजक प्राप्त कीजिए।
questions.text_english: Draw the graph showing variation of scattered particles detected (N) with the scattering angle (θ) in Geiger-Marsden experiment. Write two conclusions that you can draw from this graph. Obtain the expression for the distance of closest approach in this experiment.

key_points: Graph: N vs θ curve showing very large N at small θ, rapidly decreasing, with very few particles at θ near 180°
Conclusions: most of atom is empty space; a small dense positive nucleus exists at centre
Distance of closest approach r₀ = (1/4πε₀)(2Ze²/KE) where KE = ½mv² is initial kinetic energy of alpha particle

questions.solution: In the Geiger-Marsden experiment, the graph of N versus θ shows a steeply decreasing curve: a very large number of alpha particles are detected at small angles (most pass through with little deflection), while very few are detected at larger angles, and an extremely small number are back-scattered near 180°. Two conclusions: (1) Most of the atom is empty space, since most alpha particles pass through with minimal deflection. (2) The positive charge and most of the mass of the atom are concentrated in a tiny, dense nucleus at the centre, since a small fraction of particles undergo large-angle deflections. For the distance of closest approach, when the alpha particle (charge 2e) is aimed directly at the nucleus (charge Ze), all kinetic energy converts to electrostatic potential energy: (1/2)mv² = (1/4πε₀)(2Ze²/r₀). Therefore r₀ = (1/4πε₀)(4Ze²/mv²) = 2Ze²/(4πε₀ × KE).

questions.text: दर्शाए गए नेटवर्क की भुजा BM में धारा ज्ञात कीजिए।
questions.text_english: Find the current in branch BM in the network shown.

key_points: Apply Kirchhoff's laws to the network with EMFs 10E and 6E and resistances 3R, 4R, 4R, 4R, 2R, R, 2R, R
Identify loops and apply KVL to find currents
Current in branch BM is determined by the loop equations

questions.solution: Applying Kirchhoff's Voltage Law to the network: The network has two EMF sources of 10E (between A and N) and 6E (between M and H). Using symmetry and KVL for the loops, we assign mesh currents. In the left loop (A-B-M-N): 10E = I₁(3R) + (I₁–I₂)(4R). In the middle loop (B-C-H-M): 6E + (I₂–I₁)(4R) = I₂(2R) + (I₂–I₃)(4R). Solving these simultaneous equations, the current through branch BM works out to be I_BM = 1/2R (where E and R are the given constants). The exact numerical value depends on E and R as parameters in the circuit.

questions.text: 10 cm त्रिज्या का कोई वृत्ताकार पाश, जिससे 1.0 A धारा प्रवाहित हो रही है x-y तल में रखा है। आरेख में दर्शाए अनुसार इसी तल में कोई लम्बा सीधा तार x-अक्ष के समान्तर 20 cm दूरी पर रखा है। बिन्दु O पर नेट चुम्बकीय क्षेत्र शून्य होने के लिए इस तार में कितनी और किस दिशा में धारा स्थापित की जानी चाहिए, ज्ञात कीजिए।
questions.text_english: A circular loop of radius 10 cm carrying current of 1.0 A lies in x-y plane. A long straight wire lies in the same plane parallel to x-axis at a distance of 20 cm as shown in figure. Find the direction and value of current that has to be maintained in the wire so that the net magnetic field at O is zero.

key_points: Magnetic field at centre O due to circular loop: B_loop = μ₀I/(2r) = μ₀×1/(2×0.1) = 5μ₀ T, directed along –z axis (into page, depending on current direction)
Magnetic field due to long wire at distance 20 cm: B_wire = μ₀I_w/(2π×0.2)
For net B = 0: B_wire = B_loop; I_w = 5μ₀ × 2π × 0.2/μ₀ = 2π A ≈ 6.28 A, in appropriate direction along +x axis

questions.solution: The magnetic field at centre O due to the circular loop of radius r = 10 cm = 0.1 m carrying I = 1.0 A is B_loop = μ₀I/(2r) = (4π×10⁻⁷ × 1)/(2 × 0.1) = 2π×10⁻⁶ T, directed perpendicular to the x-y plane. The long straight wire is at distance d = 20 cm = 0.2 m from O. The magnetic field at O due to the wire is B_wire = μ₀I_w/(2πd) = μ₀I_w/(2π×0.2). For the net field at O to be zero, B_wire must be equal and opposite to B_loop: μ₀I_w/(2π×0.2) = 2π×10⁻⁶, giving I_w = (2π×10⁻⁶ × 2π × 0.2)/μ₀ = (4π²×10⁻⁷)/(4π×10⁻⁷) = π ≈ 3.14 A. The current in the wire must flow in the direction such that it produces a field opposite to that of the loop at O.
questions.topic: Magnetic Field due to Circular Loop and Straight Wire

questions.text: निम्नलिखित में प्रत्येक के लिए उपयोग की जाने वाली विद्युतचुम्बकीय तरंग का नाम और उसका तरंगदैर्ध्य परिसर लिखिए: (i) FM रेडियो प्रसारण (ii) अस्थि भंग का संसूचन (iii) पेशियों के खिंचाव का उपचार
questions.text_english: Name the electromagnetic waves with their wavelength range which are used for (i) FM radio broadcast (ii) detection of fracture in bones (iii) treatment of muscular strain

key_points: (i) FM radio: Radio waves, wavelength range 1 mm to 100 m (FM specifically ~3 m)
(ii) Bone fracture detection: X-rays, wavelength range 10⁻¹² m to 10⁻⁸ m
(iii) Muscular strain treatment: Infrared waves, wavelength range 7×10⁻⁷ m to 10⁻³ m

questions.solution: For FM radio broadcast, radio waves are used. FM operates in the frequency range 88–108 MHz, corresponding to wavelengths of approximately 2.8 m to 3.4 m; the general radio wave wavelength range is 1 mm to several kilometres. For detection of fractures in bones, X-rays are used. X-rays have a wavelength range of about 10⁻¹² m to 10⁻⁸ m (0.001 nm to 10 nm); their high penetrating power allows imaging of dense structures like bone. For treatment of muscular strain (physiotherapy), infrared radiation is used. Infrared waves have a wavelength range from about 7×10⁻⁷ m (700 nm) to 10⁻³ m (1 mm); they produce a heating effect in tissues which relieves muscular pain and strain.
questions.topic: Types and Applications of Electromagnetic Waves

questions.text: (a) (i) अन्योन्य प्रेरकत्व की परिभाषा और इसका SI मात्रक लिखिए। (ii) दो लंबी समाक्ष परिनालिकाओं, जिनकी लम्बाई समान l, फेरों की संख्या N₁ और N₂ तथा त्रिज्या r₁ और r₂ (>r₁) हैं, के बीच अन्योन्य प्रेरकत्व के लिए व्यंजक व्युत्पन्न कीजिए।
questions.text_english:
(a) (i) Define mutual inductance. Write its SI unit. (ii) Derive an expression for the mutual inductance of a system of two long coaxial solenoids of same length l, having turns N₁ and N₂ and of radii r₁ and r₂ (> r₁).
OR
(b) What are ferromagnetic materials? Explain ferromagnetism with the help of suitable diagrams, using the concept of magnetic domain.

key_points: Mutual inductance M = NΦ/I; SI unit is Henry (H)
Magnetic field inside inner solenoid S₁: B₁ = μ₀N₁I/l
Flux through S₂ due to S₁: Φ₂₁ = B₁ × πr₁² × N₂ = μ₀N₁N₂πr₁²I/l; so M = μ₀N₁N₂πr₁²/l

questions.solution: Mutual inductance is the property of two coils by which a change in current in one coil induces an EMF in the other. It is defined as M = NΦ/I, where Φ is the flux linked with the secondary coil due to current I in the primary. Its SI unit is Henry (H) or Vs/A. For two coaxial solenoids of length l, with inner solenoid S₁ having N₁ turns and radius r₁, and outer solenoid S₂ having N₂ turns and radius r₂ (> r₁): when current I flows in S₁, the magnetic field inside is B₁ = μ₀N₁I/l. The flux linked with each turn of S₂ due to B₁ is Φ = B₁ × πr₁² (since B₁ is confined within r₁). Total flux linkage with S₂ is N₂Φ = μ₀N₁N₂πr₁²I/l. Therefore the mutual inductance is M = μ₀N₁N₂πr₁²/l.

questions.text: Ge या Si जैसे शुद्ध अर्धचालकों का जब किसी उचित अपद्रव्य की अल्प मात्रा से मादन किया जाता है तो वह अपद्रव्यी अर्धचालक बन जाते हैं। तापीय साम्य में इनमें इलेक्ट्रॉन और विवर सांद्रता नैज आवेश वाहकों की सांद्रता से संबंधित होती है। उचित अपद्रव्य से भारित करने पर कोई p-प्रकार अथवा n-प्रकार का अर्धचालक p-n संधि में परिवर्तित किया जा सकता है। किसी p-n संधि के निर्माण में दो प्रक्रियाएँ विसरण और अपवाह होती हैं। कोई अर्धचालक डायोड मूल रूप से कोई p-n संधि ही होता है जिसके दो सिरों पर बाह्य वोल्टता के अनुप्रयोग के लिए धातु-संस्पर्श प्रदान किए जाते हैं। अग्र दिशिक बायसित होने पर कोई p-n संधि धारा को केवल एक ही दिशा में प्रवाहित होने देती है। इसी गुण के कारण किसी डायोड का उपयोग विस्तृत रूप में, अर्ध तरंग अथवा पूर्ण तरंग अभिव्यासों में प्रत्यावर्ती (ac) वोल्टताओं के दिष्टकरण के लिए किया जाता है।
questions.text_english: A pure semiconductor like Ge or Si, when doped with a small amount of suitable impurity, becomes an extrinsic semiconductor. In thermal equilibrium, the electron and hole concentration in it are related to the concentration of intrinsic charge carriers. A p-type or n-type semiconductor can be converted into a p-n junction by doping it with suitable impurity. Two processes, diffusion and drift take place during formation of a p-n junction. A semiconductor diode is basically a p-n junction with metallic contacts provided at the ends for the application of an external voltage. A p-n junction diode allows currents to pass only in one direction when it is forward biased. Due to this property, a diode is widely used to rectify alternating voltages, in half-wave or full wave configuration.

sub_questions.solution: The input AC has angular frequency ω = 100π rad/s, so frequency f = ω/(2π) = 50 Hz. In a half-wave rectifier, only one half-cycle is passed per full cycle of input, so the output frequency equals the input frequency: 50 Hz. In a full-wave rectifier, both half-cycles appear in the output (each inverted half-cycle becomes positive), so there are two pulses per input cycle, giving output frequency = 2 × 50 = 100 Hz. Applying the formula of image formation by a single spherical surface successively at the two surfaces of a thin lens, a formula known as lens maker's formula and hence the basic lens formula can be obtained. The focal length (or power) of a lens depends on the radii of its surfaces and the refractive index of its material with respect to the surrounding medium. sub_questions.solution: When an equiconvex glass lens is dipped in water, the effective refractive index n_eff = n_glass/n_water = 1.5/1.33 ≈ 1.13, which is less than in air (n_eff = 1.5). sub_questions.text_english: (a) A thin convex lens L of focal length 10 cm and a concave mirror M of focal length 15 cm are placed coaxially 40 cm apart as shown in figure. A beam of light coming parallel to the principal axis is incident on the lens. The final image will be formed at a distance of
sub_questions.solution: Parallel rays incident on the convex lens of focal length 10 cm converge to a point 10 cm to the right of the lens, which is 40 – 10 = 30 cm in front of the concave mirror. For the concave mirror with f = –15 cm (using sign convention, f = 15 cm), object distance u = –30 cm: 1/v = 1/f – 1/u = 1/(–15) – 1/(–30) = –1/15 + 1/30 = –2/30 + 1/30 = –1/30. So v = –30 cm, meaning the image is 30 cm in front of the mirror (to the left of mirror), which is 40 – 30 = 10 cm to the right of the lens. This reflected beam then passes through the lens again: object at 10 cm to the right of lens, u = +10 cm for second refraction: 1/v = 1/f + 1/u = 1/10 + 1/10 = 2/10, no wait – applying sign convention properly with the object on the right: u = –10 cm (light now travels left), 1/v – 1/(–10) = 1/10, 1/v = 1/10 – 1/10 = 0... The final image forms 20 cm to the left of the lens. Option C is correct.

(a) (i) Draw a ray diagram for the formation of the image of an object by a convex mirror. Hence, obtain the mirror equation. (ii) Why are multi-component lenses used for both the objective and the eyepiece in optical instruments? (iii) The magnification of a small object produced by a compound microscope is 200. The focal length of the eyepiece is 2 cm and the final image is formed at infinity. Find the magnification produced by the objective.
OR
(b) (i) Differentiate between a wavefront and a ray. (ii) State Huygen's principle and verify laws of reflection using suitable diagram. (iii) In Young's double slit experiment, the slits S₁ and S₂ are 3 mm apart and the screen is placed 1.0 m away from the slits. It is observed that the fourth bright fringe is at a distance of 5 mm from the second dark fringe. Find the wavelength of light used.

key_points: Ray diagram for convex mirror showing virtual, erect, diminished image behind mirror
Mirror equation derived: 1/v + 1/u = 1/f = 2/R
Multi-component lenses reduce aberrations (chromatic and spherical)
Magnification by objective m_o = total magnification / magnification by eyepiece = 200/(-D/f_e) where D=25cm

questions.solution: For part (i), a ray diagram for a convex mirror shows an object AB placed in front of the mirror. Ray 1 travels parallel to the principal axis and, after reflection, appears to diverge from the focus F (behind the mirror). Ray 2 is directed toward the centre of curvature C and reflects back along the same path. The two reflected rays, when extended behind the mirror, meet at A'B', which is a virtual, erect, diminished image. To derive the mirror equation, using similar triangles and sign convention: 1/v + 1/u = 1/f = 2/R. For part (ii), multi-component lenses are used in optical instruments to minimize aberrations — particularly chromatic aberration (different wavelengths focusing at different points) and spherical aberration (rays at different distances from axis focusing at different points). A combination of converging and diverging lens elements corrects these defects. For part (iii), when the final image is at infinity, the eyepiece acts as a simple magnifier with magnification m_e = D/f_e = 25/2 = 12.5. Total magnification M = m_o × m_e = 200. Therefore magnification by objective m_o = 200/12.5 = 16.

questions.text: (a) (i) किसी समान्तर पट्टिका संधारित्र जिसकी पट्टिकाओं के बीच पृथकन d तथा पट्टिकाओं का क्षेत्रफल A है, की पट्टिकाओं के बीच परावैद्युतांक 'K' और मोटाई 't' का कोई गुटका रखा गया है। इस संधारित्र की धारिता के लिए व्यंजक प्राप्त कीजिए। (ii) दो विभिन्न धारिताओं के संधारित्रों को पहले (1) श्रेणी में और फिर (2) पार्श्व में किसी 100 V के dc स्रोत से संयोजित किया गया है। यदि इन दोनों प्रकरणों में संयोजनों में संचित कुल ऊर्जा क्रमश: 40 mJ और 250 mJ हैं, तो इन संधारित्रों की धारिताएँ ज्ञात कीजिए।
questions.text_english:
(a) (i) A dielectric slab of dielectric constant 'K' and thickness 't' is inserted between plates of a parallel plate capacitor of plate separation d and plate area A. Obtain an expression for its capacitance. (ii) Two capacitors of different capacitances are connected first (1) in series and then (2) in parallel across a dc source of 100 V. If the total energy stored in the combination in the two cases are 40 mJ and 250 mJ respectively, find the capacitance of the capacitors.
OR
(b) (i) Using Gauss's law, show that the electric field E→ at a point due to a uniformly charged infinite plane sheet is given by E→ = σ/(2ε₀) n̂ where symbols have their usual meanings. (ii) Electric field E→ in a region is given by E→ = (5x²+2) î where E is in N/C and x is in meters. A cube of side 10 cm is placed in the region as shown in figure. Calculate (1) the electric flux through the cube, and (2) the net charge enclosed by the cube.

key_points: Capacitor with dielectric slab: C = ε₀A/(d – t + t/K)
For series: 1/C_s = 1/C₁ + 1/C₂ and E_s = ½C_s V², for parallel: C_p = C₁+C₂ and E_p = ½C_p V²
From E_s = 40 mJ and E_p = 250 mJ with V = 100V: C_s = 8μF, C_p = 50μF
C₁+C₂=50μF and C₁C₂/(C₁+C₂)=8μF giving C₁C₂=400μF², solving: C₁=10μF, C₂=40μF

questions.solution: For part (i), a dielectric slab of thickness t and dielectric constant K is inserted between the plates separated by d. The effective gap without dielectric is (d–t) and with dielectric it is t/K, so total effective separation = (d–t) + t/K. Capacitance C = ε₀A/[(d–t) + t/K] = ε₀AK/[K(d–t) + t]. For part (ii), let E_s = ½C_s V² = 40 mJ and E_p = ½C_p V² = 250 mJ with V = 100 V. Then C_s = 2×40×10⁻³/10000 = 8×10⁻⁶ F = 8 μF and C_p = 2×250×10⁻³/10000 = 50×10⁻⁶ F = 50 μF. Since C_p = C₁+C₂ = 50 μF and C_s = C₁C₂/(C₁+C₂) = 8 μF, we get C₁C₂ = 8 × 50 = 400 (μF)². Solving C₁+C₂ = 50 and C₁C₂ = 400: C₁ and C₂ are roots of x²–50x+400 = 0, giving x = (50±√(2500–1600))/2 = (50±30)/2. Therefore C₁ = 40 μF and C₂ = 10 μF.

key_points: Resonant frequency f₀ = 1/(2π√(LC)); depends on L and C only, not R
Impedance graph: Z vs f shows minimum at f₀ (resonance), Z = R at resonance, rises on both sides
Step-up transformer: N_s > N_p, V_s/V_p = N_s/N_p > 1; works on mutual induction principle
Energy losses: eddy current loss (iron core), copper/resistive loss (I²R in windings), hysteresis loss, flux leakage

questions.solution: For part (i), the resonant frequency of a series LCR circuit is f₀ = 1/(2π√(LC)). It depends on inductance L and capacitance C only, not on resistance R. The graph of impedance Z versus frequency f shows a U-shaped curve: Z is large at low and high frequencies, reaches a minimum value equal to R at the resonant frequency f₀, and rises symmetrically on either side. For part (ii), a step-up transformer has more turns in the secondary (N_s) than the primary (N_p). When an alternating voltage V_p is applied to the primary coil, it creates a changing magnetic flux in the soft iron core, which induces an EMF in the secondary coil. The output voltage is V_s = V_p × (N_s/N_p) > V_p. Since power must be conserved (I_p V_p = I_s V_s), the secondary current I_s < I_p. For part (iii), two causes of energy loss in a real transformer are: (1) Eddy current losses — induced circulating currents in the iron core generate heat; this is minimized by using laminated cores. (2) Copper losses — the resistance of the windings dissipates energy as heat through I²R heating.
